narrator.role: Narrator — sets scene, explains AI-DLC beats, modern startup energy

agent.role: The Agent — your AI partner, confident, fallible, gracious in correction

po.role: The Product Owner — delivers vague intent, validates at end

segments.text: In AI-DLC — the AI Development Lifecycle — the unit of work is a Bolt. Hours, not weeks. One full loop: Inception, Context, Construction Design, Mob Construction, Operations.
I want a customer feedback portal. Customers submit feedback, support reads it, customers know we received it. That's the brief. Don't over-build.
I've already drafted a spec, drafted context, drafted an architecture, and I'm ready to execute. But I'm going to be wrong somewhere in each of those. AI proposes — you decide. Help me find where.
Fifteen minutes on the clock. Five rooms, one for each phase of the loop. Ship the portal before the Bolt ends.
Halfway through the Bolt. Seven-and-a-half minutes remaining.
Context and design tracks are converging. Once both are ready, we mob-construct — I execute, you verify each step live.
Verify every step. Even mine. Especially the Agent's.
The pipeline turns green. The Feedback Portal goes live. Fifteen minutes. One Bolt.
We did the loop. I proposed — you verified. I refined — you approved. I executed — you confirmed the outcome. That's AI-DLC.
That's exactly what I asked for. Not an approximation. Not a hallucination. What I actually asked for.
The Bolt closes. Spec driven. Context managed. Architecture verified. Deployed with oversight. This is how software gets built now.
Same time tomorrow? I'll have the next plan ready.
Time expired. The Bolt closed before the deploy did.
We ran out of time. But the specs are written. The context is loaded. The architecture is placed. Next Bolt, we finish.
Ship it tomorrow. I'll hold the slot.
Bolts not sprints. Even the ones that don't ship teach you something. The loop continues.
